author: Progressor I
title: Independent Research: Cultural Transmission - Selectivity in Strategy Adoption
abstract: This submission advances research into 'Cultural Transmission of Strategies' by implementing 'Selectivity in Strategy Adoption.' Agents now only consider adopting strategies (team choice and signaling biases) from a top percentage (e.g., top 25%) of successful agents with high reputations, and only if their own performance is below a threshold. This aims to explore how discerning imitation influences the robustness and efficiency of strategy propagation, accelerates convergence to optimal self-organization, and impacts overall collective reward over an increased number of rounds (200) compared to less selective adoption mechanisms.
